newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields edge lower,trade still light.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields edge lower,trade still light.

text.p: *Australian bond yields edged lower, but trading remained relatively light in the absence of a guiding light from the U.S. market, which was closed on Monday.
*Q1 capital expenditure due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields edged lower, but trading remained relatively light in the absence of a guiding light from the U.S. market, which was closed on Monday.
Traders reported domestic buying of the front end of the bond curve, which was seen as offering some value after last week's official interest rate cut to 5.5 percent.

"The three year bond is 100 basis points over cash. Given that 5.5 percent is going to be here for a while and that we were 70 to 80 over before the rate cut, it's looking a safe bet for the moment," one trader said.

The market sees its first data of the week with the release of first quarter capital expenditure at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Forecasts centre on a 3.5 percent rise after the 2.4 percent fall in the December quarter, but of more importance will be the second estimate for investment spending in 1997/98 as a clue to future growth, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

However, traders said that as the data will largely be historical it is not expected to have much impact on the market, and more emphasis would be put on the activity indicators, such as retail trade data, which are due later this week for the April period.

The firm tone saw spreads to the dollar bloc narrow, and the three-year differential to the U.S. close in on parity again, having briefly tested it in immediate reaction on the rate cut on Friday. With the emphasis on short end, the local yield curve steepened once again.
